findings.summary: Two measurement-coverage reductions ride the adopted skin, both below medium and both consequences of the authorized hairline aesthetic rather than threshold weakening. (a) The prior instrument pinned 'strong line on black' (old --line-strong #58616f, ui 3.0); the adopted skin redefines --line/--line-strong as rgba(255,255,255,0.09/0.17), which the hex-only parser cannot represent, so no border/divider token is measured at all — the 0.17-alpha hairline blends to roughly 1.9:1 over black, below the 3.0 non-text bar of WCAG 1.4.11 where a border is the sole component boundary cue. (b) The prior stylesheet applied the custom focus outline to button, input, select, a, summary, and [tabindex]:focus-visible (237ee69 styles.css:66-73); the adopted skin styles only button:focus-visible (styles.css:52-55). No outline suppression exists anywhere, so inputs/textareas/selects fall back to the user-agent default focus ring — visible, but no longer the measured red indicator. Text-token coverage (the invariant-5 contract) is complete; these are non-text-UI residuals.
findings.title: Instrument no longer measures any hairline/border token and custom focus ring narrowed to buttons
